title: Simple Sorting
description: Learn the basic mechanics of simple sorting algorithms such as Bubble Sort and Selection Sort.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Sorting is the process of arranging data into a specific order.

Many algorithms become more efficient when data is organized properly.

Simple sorting algorithms help students understand how elements can be compared, swapped, and rearranged systematically.

sections.title: Why Sorting Matters
sections.content:
Sorted data is easier to search, analyze, and process efficiently.

Applications such as online stores, ranking systems, and databases rely heavily on sorting algorithms.

Although advanced sorting methods exist, simple sorting algorithms provide an important introduction to algorithmic thinking.

sections.title: Bubble Sort
sections.content:
Bubble Sort repeatedly compares neighboring elements and swaps them if they are in the wrong order.

After each pass, larger values gradually move toward the end of the collection.

This process continues until the entire dataset becomes sorted.

Although Bubble Sort is easy to understand, it becomes inefficient for large datasets because it requires many repeated comparisons.

sections.title: Selection Sort
sections.content:
Selection Sort works by repeatedly finding the smallest remaining element and placing it into its correct position.

The algorithm divides the array into sorted and unsorted regions.

During each iteration, the smallest value from the unsorted region is selected and moved into the sorted portion.

sections.title: Comparing Bubble Sort and Selection Sort
sections.content:
Both Bubble Sort and Selection Sort are simple quadratic-time algorithms.

Bubble Sort performs many swaps between neighboring elements, while Selection Sort focuses on selecting the correct element during each iteration.

Although neither algorithm is ideal for large-scale systems, they are valuable educational tools for understanding sorting behavior.

sections.title: Sorting in Real Applications
sections.content:
Sorting algorithms are widely used in databases, search engines, recommendation systems, and operating systems.

Even though modern applications often use advanced sorting algorithms, understanding simple sorting methods helps students build a strong foundation in algorithm design and performance analysis.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
sections.content: Simple sorting algorithms arrange data into an organized order through repeated comparisons and swaps. Bubble Sort and Selection Sort introduce important algorithm concepts such as iteration, comparison, and data movement.
